quotes.text: Stripe and PayPal review each request, which can take several weeks.
After your request is approved, you receive instructions for connecting your PayPal account.
Because PayPal doesn’t support direct charges or `on_behalf_of`, you don’t need to enable it on connected accounts’ payment method configurations.
You can submit evidence to contest a dispute directly from the Stripe Dashboard.
PayPal doesn’t have a minimum charge amount, but Stripe enforces the same

old_evidence.text: Stripe sends email updates about the progress of all requests
PayPal isn’t available for platforms that onboard other businesses and enable them to accept payments directly

findings: Both dates cover the standard Stripe-processed PayPal offering for merchants in the enumerated European countries and worldwide customers, 14 presentment currencies and standard payout timing. The account/customer geographic distinction and separate own-PayPal-account or outside-country custom payment route matter.

The customer selects PayPal, signs in after redirect, selects a wallet, linked card/account or BNPL funding method and authorizes; the merchant receives immediate success/failure notification. The prose describes a successful redirect back, while both detailed flows label a merchant-site visit optional; buyer return should be kept separate from outcome notification.

November specifies marketplace Dashboard Request access plus form, joint Stripe/PayPal review over potentially several weeks, settings status and post-approval PayPal-account connection instructions. Destination and separate charges/transfers remain supported; Direct and on_behalf_of remain unsupported. It explicitly says enablement in connected-account payment method configurations is unnecessary.

Both capture dates support full/partial refunds through Stripe Dashboard or API within 180 days, with settlement preference driving Stripe funds or PayPal balance/other available PayPal funding. Stripe Dashboard is the evidence submission surface; PayPal Dashboard is for direct customer contact in applicable dispute types. Preserve the PayPal-provided eligibility limitation on Seller Protection.

Both enumerate the same 30 European business country codes, including GB, CH, NO and LI, as counted in the mapped source and wallets concept. Some inbound routes narrow this to EU merchants. PayPal has no separate minimum, while Stripe’s general minimum and maximum apply.
CDN URLs replace local asset paths with identical captured payment-flow captions and order. Heading/table formatting and the Seller Protection buyer/customer wording are presentation.

Ordinary standard PayPal go-live uses the activation route from payment method settings. The possible recurring approval is a separate qualification. Only qualifying Connect marketplaces use the additional marketplace request and approval-to-connection process.
substantive_changes: Add November marketplace request form, joint reviewer and non-SLA time estimate, tracked status, approval-to-connection instructions and no need for connected-account configuration. Preserve May's email update text as May-only unless reverified.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May’s onboarding request, manual approval and progress emails are historical documentation, and both dates describe Dashboard progress and marketplace-only charge types.

Both dates retain recurring access possibly requiring approval, standard payout timing, 180-day refund eligibility, conditional funding by settlement preferences, report/tax-invoice distinction and PayPal Seller Protection only for eligible transactions.
The same 30 European locations are documented on both dates, and there is no geography expansion. Stripe's general charge bounds apply in both dates; PayPal has no separate minimum.
conflicts: Old raw lines 56–85 and new raw lines 57–86 both list the same 30 country codes, consistent with the mapped source and concept count. Inbound Wallets, PayPal index, Stripe company and custom-PayPal source labels saying EU or EU-only over-narrow the documented European list.
Mapped source line 35 already mentions the Stripe minimum and maximum in parentheses. Clarify in the main label that absence of a separate minimum applies to PayPal.

Both raws describe a successful redirect back in the intro but mark customer return to the merchant site optional in the illustrated flow. Preserve outcome notification and observed page-return descriptions separately.
unresolved_questions: November does not repeat May’s email updates and does not establish their removal. Several weeks is a documented possibility rather than a guarantee or proof of account approval.
Uninspected CDN illustrations and linked CPM/activation/disputes pages cannot establish image differences or additional implementation and live eligibility within this packet.

findings: Retain the accurate 30-country count. Add November marketplace onboarding and account-scoped guidance, specify that PayPal has no independent minimum and Stripe's limits still apply, and preserve the existing dated refund and dispute boundaries.
conflicts: Source line 17 correctly counts 30. Its inbound EU-only shorthand is narrower than the captured European list. Lines 23 and 27 omit November onboarding detail and the dated alternate refund-funding qualification.
source_assessments.reason: The updated marketplace prerequisites are action-relevant. Clarify the external routes’ geographic shorthand and identify which party sets charge limits.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal, source-stripe-paypal.md covers Stripe-processed PayPal for buyers worldwide at listed European merchant locations. Old raw lines 8–22 and 96–112 and new raw lines 9–23 and 97–112 cover PayPal authentication after redirect, customer-selected funding and immediate merchant success/failure notification, with the return visit marked optional in the illustration. Ordinary merchants follow the go-live PayPal activation route in old raw lines 126–130 and new raw lines 137–141. Recurring payments can require separate approval under old raw lines 38–42 and new raw lines 39–43. Old raw lines 114–124 and new raw lines 114–135 restrict Connect to online marketplaces and destination or separate charges/transfers. November describes Dashboard form submission, Stripe and PayPal review, status tracking, approval, PayPal account connection and the connected-account configuration exemption. Old raw lines 132–148 and new raw lines 143–159 retain 180-day settlement-routed refunds, Stripe Dashboard dispute evidence and PayPal Dashboard contact for applicable disputes.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal, source-stripe-paypal.md should add the action-relevant joint review, potential several-week timing and approval-to-connection step from new raw lines 118–129 while dating request progress emails to old raw lines 114–118. Flow asset paths, heading formatting and buyer/customer terms are presentation changes. Old raw lines 56–85 and new raw lines 57–86 have the same 30 supported business-country codes, including non-EU CH, GB, LI and NO. Preserve the count and correct the narrower inbound EU-only shorthand and distinguish PayPal’s absent minimum from Stripe’s continued limits under old raw lines 158–160 and new raw lines 169–171.
